sentences.text:
This is the first bail application filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C., who is in custody since 06.09.2021 in connection with Crime No.438/2021 registered at Police Station Gwarighat,
District Jabalpur (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 468, 471 of IPC, Sections 51, 52 of Food Safety Standard Act, 2006 and Sections 103, 104 of Trademark Act, 1999.

Prosecution story, in brief, is that on 16.07.2021 proprietor of Shree Hari Products, applicant was found engaged in packaging of various packets of gulab jamun, adulterated and misbranded spices i.e. cumin and loose coconut power without any license.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that none of the alleged offences are made out against the applicant and ingredients of Sections 420, 468 & 471 of IPC are not being fulfilled.

Offences punishable under Section 51 and 52 of Food Safety Act, 2006 are punishable only with fine,
therefore, the applicant cannot be detained in custody.
Applicant has certificate with regard to the manufacture of the said material.
He is about 55 years old.
Co-accused person, who is the son of the applicant has already been granted bail by this Court in MCRC No.37441/2021 on 13.08.2021 and case of the present applicant is akin to that co-accused.
Charge-sheet has been filed.
He is in judicial custody since 06.09.2021.
Due to Covid-19 Pandemic, trial will take time to conclude, therefore, he may be enlarged on bail.

Per contra, learned counsel for the State has opposed the application 2 MCRC-47233-2021 and submitted that report of State Food Testing Laboratory has been received, in which it is clearly mentioned that material seized from the possession of applicant was misbranded, therefore, the applicant may not be enlarged on bail.

Having considered the rival submissions and considering the allegations alleged against the Ashok Nagrani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 October, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2553271/
1 applicant and also looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the considered view that it is a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.

sentences.text: Hence, without commenting anything on merits of the matter, this application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court for his appearance before the trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the trial Court during the pendency of the trial.

It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
I n view of the outbreak of 'Corona Virus disease (COVID-19)' the concerned jail authorities are directed to follow the directions/guidelines issued by the Government with regard to 'COVID-19'
before releasing the applicant.

This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.
Certified copy as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR (VERMA)) JUDGE vc Ashok Nagrani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 October, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2553271/
